Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
Rejoinder affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
3. No one appears on behalf of the respondent complainant despite service of notice.

4.In terms of the F.I.R. lodged on 28.1.2024, it was alleged that the victim became friendly to the applicant in February, 2020 and on 19.3.2020, when she was alone, the applicant got the ice-cream and after eating the icre-cream, she became unconscious and rape was committed on her.
Subsequently, on the basis of indecent videos, the rape was again committed on her on 25.6.2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that there is an inordinate delay in lodging the F.I.R.
There is no recovery of any mobile or video to demonstrate or prove the allegation of blackmailing.
The age of the victim is 37 years.
Hence, the applicant who is languishing in jail since 30.1.2024 having criminal history of one case in which the applicant is on bail, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

7. Considering the fact that there is an inordinate delay in lodging the F.I.R; there is no recovery of any mobile or video to demonstrate or prove the allegation of blackmailing; the age of the victim is 37 years coupled with the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 30.1.2024 having criminal history of one case in which the applicant is on bail, without expressing any opinion on merits, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant Nihal@ Sayyad Abdul Alim Jafri be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.41 of 2024, under Sections 328, 376-D, 406 I.P.C. and Section 3/5 (1) of U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, Police Station Ghazipur, District Lucknow on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
